entities.name: Emrakul
entities.description: One of the three legendary Eldrazi; her name is linguistic residue from the Eldrazi's first rising on Zendikar and became confused with the 'god' Emeria.

entities.name: Ulamog
entities.description: One of the three legendary Eldrazi; his name became woven into the Zendikari legend of the 'god' Ula.

entities.name: Kozilek
entities.description: One of the three legendary Eldrazi; his name became woven into the Zendikari legend of the 'god' Cosi.

entities.name: Eldrazi
entities.description: Alien beings whose consciousness is too strange for Zendikar's inhabitants to understand; they arose once more on Zendikar after rising thousands of years earlier.

entities.name: Zendikar
entities.description: The plane whose peoples worshipped patron deities that turned out to be tied to the Eldrazi.

entities.name: Emeria, Ula, and Cosi
entities.description: The 'gods' of Zendikari legend, patron deities worshipped by some peoples, that are bastardized memories of the three Eldrazi.

entities.name: Merfolk of Zendikar
entities.description: Zendikari people whose old phrases may be the source of the Eldrazi names and who came to understand the mistake of worshipping the deities.

events.summary: The Eldrazi arise once more on Zendikar, and the merfolk realize they had mistaken the Eldrazi names for the legends of gods.
events.quote: But as the Eldrazi arose once more, the merfolk came to understand their mistake.

events.summary: The columnist explains that Zendikari are unlikely to have understood any Eldrazi communication, so the Eldrazi did not introduce themselves.
events.quote: The Eldrazi consciousness is too alien, too starkly different for our forms of language to latch on to their forms of awareness.

relations.note: The legends of these 'gods' grew from bastardized memories of the three legendary Eldrazi.
relations.quote: becoming woven into the legends of "gods" called Emeria, Ula, and Cosi.
